meta.notes: One block per scenario in data/scenarios/. Provenance is copied from the JSON file; config.describe() and the layer description come from the loaded SimConfig. 100 replicates per scenario, first seed 0, stride 1. Flow conservation and finiteness are asserted for every replicate, so a scenario that fails would abort this script instead of appearing here. The balk decision uses the engine's wait estimate divided by the number of staff units ON SHIFT at the arrival instant (shift windows and breaks are coverage-checked), so scenarios with late shift starts, breaks or a mid-shift joiner are not credited with absent staff; the stationary baseline path keeps the full worker count so the baseline anchors stay bit-identical. Note: sla.fairness_cap_minutes in a scenario file is an alias for the policy starvation cap, so peak_pricing/strict_sla_fairness behave as their provenance describes.

scenarios.name: baseline_flat
scenarios.title: baseline: flat demand, one clerk pool, fixed service times

provenance.source: Course 5006 project assumptions (report and experiment ledger)
provenance.method: Direct copy of the baseline configuration; the loader must reproduce the baseline anchors bit-for-bit
provenance.notes: This file intentionally enables none of the mechanism layers; it exists to prove backward compatibility.

scenarios.name: bread_counter_bottleneck
scenarios.title: Bread counter bottleneck: one toaster slot, bread-heavy order mix

provenance.source: Synthetic: Course 5006 service-time structure with an assumed single-slot toaster/warmer, plus teaching-case ranges for bakery-attach rates
provenance.method: Bread make time raised to 1.5 min per portion at a single-slot counter, bread share raised to 45% of orders, two cashiers and two tea slots so the bread counter is the structural bottleneck
provenance.notes: Not field-measured. The bread counter and the tills are staffed by the same cashier role, so adding a second bread slot is an equipment decision, not a hiring one; the network study uses this to separate equipment capacity from labour capacity.

scenarios.name: campus_rush
scenarios.title: Campus shop: lunch and after-class peaks, group orders

provenance.source: Course 5006 assumptions (order mix, service times, prices) + typical queuing-shop peak-to-average ranges reported in operations-management teaching cases
provenance.method: Synthetic: peak multipliers and batch sizes chosen to bracket a campus day; daily mean normalised to the quoted arrival rate
provenance.notes: Not field-measured. Peaks are 1.6-1.7x the daily mean; batch arrivals represent student groups. Three tea stations + three baristas make the peaks feasible but tight.

scenarios.name: cbd_commute
scenarios.title: CBD commuter shop: short morning grab-and-go peak plus a lunch peak

provenance.source: Synthetic, anchored on the Course 5006 parameter set (order mix, make times, prices) and on teaching-case ranges for commuter-district peak-to-average ratios
provenance.method: Piecewise-constant demand from an assumed commuter day (soft open, sharp 120-minute morning peak, midday trough, lunch peak, soft close); daily mean normalised to the quoted rate; stations and staff sized so the peaks are feasible but tight
provenance.notes: Not field-measured. The morning peak is shorter and sharper than the lunch peak; peak segments run ~1.8x the daily mean. Ten-hour modelled day so both peaks fit. Batches are small (commuters rarely arrive in groups).

scenarios.name: exam_week
scenarios.title: Exam week: a much sharper student peak, extra rented tea slots

provenance.source: Synthetic, anchored on the Course 5006 parameter set and on teaching-case ranges for event-driven demand spikes
provenance.method: Same campus structure as campus_rush but with 2.0x peak-to-mean demand shape and shorter peak windows; an extra rented tea slot and a sixth staff member are added so the shop still serves most of the peak
provenance.notes: Not field-measured. Peak multiplier 2.4 on a daily mean of ~1.21 multipliers gives a peak-to-mean ratio near 2.0: the peak hour looks like a normal campus rush but the daily average is much lower, so average utilisation looks safe while abandonment spikes. Same five staff and three tea slots as campus_rush (no extra capacity is bought for the two-week window).

scenarios.name: flagship_five_staff
scenarios.title: Flagship branch: five staff, two ice slots, two bread counters, steady traffic

provenance.source: Synthetic, anchored on the Course 5006 parameter set and on teaching-case ranges for a high-volume flagship branch
provenance.method: Higher daily mean than the campus shop with a lunch peak, two ice slots and two bread counters so the extra capacity is visible in the station table; five staff with staggered breaks
provenance.notes: Not field-measured. Nine-hour day (540 min). The design intent is a shop where labour is the planned constraint and equipment is deliberately over-provisioned, the mirror image of network_tea_bottleneck and bread_counter_bottleneck.

scenarios.name: ice_cream_bottleneck
scenarios.title: Ice-cream machine bottleneck: one slow soft-serve slot, iced and mixed orders dominate

provenance.source: Synthetic: Course 5006 service-time structure with an assumed slow soft-serve machine, plus teaching-case ranges for cold-drink shares in warm weather
provenance.method: Ice make time raised to 1.2 min per portion (soft-serve draw plus topping), ice/mixed share raised to 60% of orders, one ice slot; tea capacity and staff left generous so the ice slot is the structural bottleneck
provenance.notes: Not field-measured. Designed as the counterpart of network_tea_bottleneck: same shop, different binding equipment. Used by the network study to test whether fast-item priority is still worth it when the bottleneck is not the tea station.

scenarios.name: inventory_generous
scenarios.title: Generous inventory: high stock cover, short lead times, visible perishable waste

provenance.source: Synthetic, anchored on the Course 5006 Lecture 4 (BOM/MRP/CRP) assumptions and on teaching-case (s, S) ranges
provenance.method: Same BOM and product structure as inventory_lean, but with 2-3x the stock cover, 30-minute replenishment lead times and a shorter pearl shelf life so the policy is generous against stock-outs yet still wastes perishables
provenance.notes: Not field-measured. Deliberate contrast to inventory_lean: fill rate should sit at (or near) 1.0 while waste is non-zero, which is the trade-off the inventory study is after. The 360-minute pearl shelf life and the large opening lots are the mechanism that makes over-stocking visible: a generous (s, S) policy buys availability with opening stock and perishable waste.

scenarios.name: inventory_lean
scenarios.title: Lean inventory: pearls perish, deliveries take two hours

provenance.source: Course 5006 Lecture 4 (BOM/MRP/CRP) assumptions + synthetic replenishment parameters
provenance.method: Synthetic: (s, S) review with 2-hour lead time and a 4-hour pearl shelf life; recipes are one kit per component
provenance.notes: Designed so that stock-outs and pearl waste actually occur at the modelled demand; not calibrated to a real supplier.

scenarios.name: late_night_study
scenarios.title: Late-night study cafe: low, long traffic with a midnight bump

provenance.source: Synthetic, anchored on the Course 5006 parameter set and on teaching-case ranges for all-night study venues
provenance.method: Twelve-hour modelled night with a small daily mean, two peaks (early evening and around midnight) and long quiet stretches; one cashier and one barista on shift for the whole night
provenance.notes: Not field-measured. The point of the scenario is the opposite of the campus rush: utilisation stays low, waiting is near the process floor, and the binding constraint is staffing (a single barista) rather than demand. Long run (720 min) makes the low-rate Poisson noise relatively less dominant.

scenarios.name: mall_weekend
scenarios.title: Weekend mall shop: afternoon and evening family peaks, group orders

provenance.source: Synthetic, anchored on the Course 5006 parameter set and on teaching-case ranges for shopping-centre weekend traffic
provenance.method: Piecewise-constant demand with a slow opening, afternoon peak, dinner dip and evening peak; daily mean normalised to the quoted rate; batch arrivals model families and friend groups; four baristas and three tea slots so the evening peak is tight but finite
provenance.notes: Not field-measured. Twelve-hour modelled day (720 min). Group orders (20% of arrivals, mean 2.5 people) are the main reason the peak rate exceeds the daily mean on a per-person basis. Two ice slots represent a larger mall counter.

scenarios.name: network_tea_bottleneck
scenarios.title: Single tea station as the bottleneck (staff-rich, equipment-poor)

provenance.source: Course 5006 flow rates + synthetic capacity assumption
provenance.method: Synthetic: one tea station and one barista, two cashiers and two order counters; demand flat so the bottleneck is structural, not demand-driven
provenance.notes: Designed to test whether fast-item triage still helps when the tea station is the binding constraint.

scenarios.name: peak_pricing
scenarios.title: Peak pricing: +30% inside the two demand peaks, elastic demand response

provenance.source: Synthetic, anchored on the Course 5006 campus demand shape and on teaching-case ranges for food-service peak surcharges and price elasticities
provenance.method: campus_rush demand shape with a +30% price inside the two peak windows and a constant-elasticity response (elasticity -1.2, i.e. a 30% surcharge removes about 27% of peak demand); the quoted arrival rate is the no-pricing daily mean, so the realised mean is lower
provenance.notes: Not field-measured. The elasticity is an assumption, not an estimate; the point is the mechanism (peak demand deflation) and the trade-off between peak waiting relief and revenue. Because the price layer changes the realised daily mean, compare it against campus_rush on served/profit/p95, not on the quoted arrival rate.

scenarios.name: rainy_delivery
scenarios.title: Rainy weekday, delivery-dominant: walk-in demand falls, rider orders take over

provenance.source: Synthetic, anchored on the Course 5006 parameter set and on teaching-case ranges for rainy-day channel shift
provenance.method: Flat-ish baseline demand with a mild lunch bump; half of all arrivals are delivery orders (no balking, higher icy/mixed mix, top queue priority), the walk-in half has low patience; two ice slots because cold drinks dominate on a wet day
provenance.notes: Not field-measured. Rain is modelled only as a channel mix shift, not as a change in total demand. The delivery class carries a heavier mixed/iced order mix, which raises make work per customer relative to a dry walk-in day. Delivery orders never balk and never renege by construction of the engine.

scenarios.name: strict_sla_fairness
scenarios.title: Strict SLA with a fairness cap: 4-minute promise, 3-unit compensation, 2-minute ageing cap

provenance.source: Synthetic, anchored on the Course 5006 campus demand shape and on teaching-case service-guarantee / compensation policies
provenance.method: campus_rush load with a 4-minute SLA target and 3-unit per-late-customer compensation, plus a 2-minute starvation cap so any job (including the low-priority tea queue) is aged to the top after two minutes; split delivery keeps the ice component of mixed orders moving
provenance.notes: Not field-measured. The SLA promise is deliberately stricter than the process can hold at the peak, so the interesting output is the compensation bill and the gap between classes, not a 100% attainment rate. The ageing cap is the fairness mechanism: it trades some fast-item speed for bounded worst-case waiting.

scenarios.name: tiny_two_staff
scenarios.title: Two-person corner shop: every station has one slot, both staff are generalists

provenance.source: Synthetic, anchored on the Course 5006 parameter set and on the teaching-case description of a small owner-operated counter
provenance.method: Two cross-trained staff with the 'all' skill, one slot per station (single tea machine, single ice machine, one till, one bread warmer); low arrival rate with a lunch bump; daily mean normalised to the quoted rate
provenance.notes: Not field-measured. With two generalists the *station* capacities bind before the labour does: the single tea slot is the equipment bottleneck at the lunch bump even though total staff utilisation stays near 60-70%. Good contrast case for the network study.
